exposure: Maternal pre-existing atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD), defined as myocardial infarction, ischemic stroke, or angina prior to conception
outcome: Neonatal complications (congenital malformations, sepsis, neonatal intensive care unit admission)
Neurodevelopmental disorders (developmental delay, seizure, attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder)
cohort: The study included 5,461,222 live births from 3,640,815 unique mothers in South Korea, of which 145,315 (2.7%) were delivered by women with pre-existing ASCVD before pregnancy.
finding: Maternal pre-existing ASCVD is independently associated with consistent increases in neonatal complications (congenital malformations, NICU admission, sepsis) and early childhood neurodevelopmental disorders in offspring.
followup_time: Up to 15 years (births between 2005-2019, followed through 2020)
